verdict.rationale: Loops has no documented built-in natural-language interface. Instead, users get natural-language operation through their own AI agents: an official MCP server reads and writes contacts, events, lists, transactional email and content, and a one-command CLI-plus-skills install lets a coding agent "use Loops for you," with an example of an agent migrating sends and templates. Workflow graphs can also be created and edited from code, which an agent could drive, but the docs frame this as programmatic access rather than an MCP tool. This delivers the story only through external agent clients. Missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language command interface, explicit agent coverage of workflow editing, and independent or hands-on evidence that natural-language operation works in practice.
